newsitem.title: USA: Nellcor Puritan down on earnings.
newsitem.headline: Nellcor Puritan down on earnings.

text.p: Shares in medical ventilator maker Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc fell sharply on Tuesday, after the company reported lower-than-expected quarterly earnings.
The Pleasanton, Calif., company's stock was down 5-5/8 to 18-1/8 in midafternoon trade, close to a 12-month low of 17-1/2. Volume was heavy and the shares were among the most active on the Nasdaq.
Nellcor reported a net loss of $0.06 a share for the second quarter, down from a profit of $0.30 for the same period in 1995.
The company had a second quarter operating profit of $0.20 a share after merger and related charges, down from $0.30 in the year-earlier period.
John Boettiger, an analyst with Houston's Harris Webb & Garrison, called the results "disappointing earnings in general."
However, he added that Nellcor faced potential trouble from distribution of its equipment under its new plan to rely on a company network rather than using distributors.
The problem could be especially acute in Japan, where their newly acquired Infrasonics unit relied on entirely on independent distributors and had a substantial market share.
"I would assume they are going to lose the bulk of those sales," he said, adding that Nellcor's own distribution network apparently had a shortage of personnel.
However, Nellcor remained the strongest producer of medical ventilators and Boettiger said the shares were attractive at $18 or $19.
"They are still the biggest and baddest across all lines of ventilators," he said.
The decline in the share price also followed a downgrade by J.P. Morgan Securities analyst Michael Weinstein, who cut Nellcor to market performer from buy.
